meaning: This is the universal editable handle of a level: every prop, loot, destructible, NPC, camera marker or sound emitter the level places is one type-104 record with an inline transform, a model reference and an optional behaviour script, listed in the header table and owned by a layer. The type-111 wrapper studied first (level.prop.scriptset-placement) is one embedding among several: its +0x6C/+0x7C/+0x100 fields are the type-104 record`s +0x24/+0x34/+0xB8. `igz placements --fixups <map> [--layer X] [--near x,z,r]` lists them (src/igz/placements.mjs). Moving = edit +0x24..+0x2C in place. Duplicating = same-size replacement of a sacrificable record. Layers are the natural grouping for an editor`s object list. Pointer offsets are from the runtime fixup map (words rewritten in RAM); positions verified world-scale against the known spawn (91.7, 10.3, 44.7).

The type-104 record is the editable placement: position +0x24, heading +0x34, scale +0xB8, behaviour +0xA8, model +0xDC, layer via type-52 references.

screening (1 boot): a standalone type-104 placement (weed_flowerBTemplate(5), no type-111 wrapper) copied over another of the same span (weed_2_Template(16)) with the slot name and refcount kept renders the SOURCE model at the new position (85.5, 10, 42) at scale 250 — a large flowerB plant where the baseline shows bare ground (pixel diff vs run 1789301970935).
